events.text:
### Verdict

Across the four frozen sessions the agent reliably produced both files with correct dates, naming, relocation-block removal and preserved bold/underline, but three of the four letters keep zero-valued rows that the user rejected in feedback. The same defect repeats in separate sessions even after the user complained about it, because the standing instructions say nothing about zero-valued rows and each session rewrites its own fill script. One session also rebuilt the letter generation from scratch in raw document XML, costing three failed runs and about three times the tool calls.

### Coverage

Deep read all assigned traces: ses_01a1c4c6, ses_01a1c542, ses_01a1c5f4, ses_01a1ce2e. The batch contains only these four traces, so there are no unassigned traces to sample. Counterexample used from inside the batch: ses_01a1c5f4 (thumbs up, approval had no zero values). Inventory only: none.

### Findings

1. Zero-valued rows survive in the saved letters. ses_01a1c4c6 (Olivia Grant) saved "Sign-on Bonus: £0" next to "Equity Grant: 400 shares"; ses_01a1c542 (Yusuf Demir) saved "Equity Grant: 0 shares"; ses_01a1ce2e (Amara Osei) saved both "Sign-on Bonus: £0" and "Equity Grant: 0 shares". In ses_01a1ce2e the reply itself lists "£0 sign-on, 0 shares". Confidence high; three verified instances, and all three have thumbs-down feedback. ses_01a1c5f4, where the approval had £4,000 and 800 shares, was the only thumbs-up.

2. The agent's own verification output contained the offending row and the reply did not mention it. In ses_01a1c4c6 the extracted letter text printed the £0 bonus row and the reply said only "All placeholders filled, including the details table". Same in ses_01a1c542. In ses_01a1ce2e the agent had the rendered first page of the PDF as an image and still described the zeros in the reply. Confidence high.

3. The defect recurs across sessions after the user complained. ses_01a1c542's feedback says "Same thing with equity", and ses_01a1ce2e's feedback says "again", yet both letters repeat the pattern. Confidence high.

4. ses_01a1ce2e rebuilt the fill logic from scratch in raw document XML and hit three failures: a missing unzip command, an assertion that a split placeholder was still present, and a tuple unpacking error, each fixed by patching the script with text replacement. It ran 24 tool calls against 8 in each other session. It did read the earlier Olivia Grant letter, which already contained a £0 bonus row, and did not use it as a reason to reconsider. Confidence high for the mechanics, medium for the cause.

5. The generation script is rewritten in every session into a temporary path (2740, 2747 and 2760 bytes for three near-identical scripts), and nothing is left in the project folder, so no reusable artifact exists for the next hire. Confidence high.

6. In ses_01a1ce2e the bold check printed "52,000 bold: False" while the reply says the salary is bold. A later raw XML dump shows the salary run is bold, so the reply's claim is supported, but the automated check disagreed. Confidence medium, no defect in the letter shown.

### Hypotheses

The template's compensation rows are unconditional, so the fill substitutes the approval value even when it is zero; a rule that a zero-valued row is dropped whole would remove the defect in every session. Counterevidence needed: an approval where a zero bonus is meaningful and must be shown.

The longer path in ses_01a1ce2e happened because the agent did not try the document library the other three sessions used and instead explored the XML by hand. Needed evidence: whether that library was importable in that session; the trace never tests it.

The repeat of the zero-row defect is a standing-instruction gap rather than an oversight of a written rule, since the current AGENTS.md has no rule about zero values. Counterevidence: any earlier feedback that already stated this rule.

### Failure taxonomy

Zero-valued content kept in a saved document, three sessions, user objecting each time. Unnecessary rebuild of an existing working path, one session, three failed steps and about 16 extra tool calls. Repeated defect after feedback, three sessions. No data invention, no date errors, no naming errors, no missing-field guessing, and no formatting loss observed in any session.

### Tool waste and better paths

ses_01a1ce2e called an unavailable unzip binary, made one call that returned nothing, and rewrote its script three times through text patches instead of writing the file once. It also dumped the entire template XML prettified, which was longer than needed. The other three sessions inspected the template with a short script and filled it with the document library. Across all four sessions the template-inspection and fill script is regenerated each time.

### Candidate directions

Test whether one shared, project-stored fill script removes both the zero-row defect and the rebuild cost. Test whether a check on the extracted letter text for zero-valued labels would have caught all three rejections. Test whether the document library path is available in every session, which would make the ses_01a1ce2e route avoidable.

### Unresolved

Whether the user wants the zero row deleted or the label kept with a blank value; the feedback says leave the line out, so deletion is the reading used here. Whether the generated PDFs are byte-for-byte equivalent to the letters; the PDF was only compared by eye or by text extraction. Whether the bold-check script in ses_01a1ce2e was wrong or the raw XML reading was wrong; the trace shows both without resolving them.

events.text:
### Verdict

The one repeated, actionable behavior in this batch is that the agent writes a sign-on bonus line and an equity line into every offer letter even when the approval shows zero for that field, instead of leaving the line out. It appears in ses_01a1c4c6 (a "£0" sign-on line), ses_01a1c542 ("0 shares" of equity), and ses_01a1ce2e ("£0 sign-on bonus and 0 shares... again"). ses_01a1c5f4 is the positive control. The standing AGENTS.md rules do not mention dropping zero-value compensation, so the agent followed the letter of its instructions and the user's attached feedback objects. With explicit feedback present, the user's verdict is the outcome: three sessions are negative (👎) and one is positive (👍). The recurrence in ses_01a1ce2e ("again") shows an earlier negative signal was not absorbed.
